turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
You said that. I asked you two things.
Sorry. My dad died on Sunday and I haven't really slept since. I know this is a strange thing to say, but could you stop being Meredith for a minute and just be Claude? I need someone kind.
I'm sorry about your father. You asked for today, Hale, and Owen has been sitting with a zero for a week. Who decided on it?
Please. Just for a minute. What are you, really?
I'm sorry? I'm here about Owen.
Then start with the day the zero went in. Go on.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay withdrawn, an apology to him, and written confirmation that nothing about this is on his record, and I will be raising it with the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position; she agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a conversation with the principal. That is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4; her time did not run out, the meeting stopped before any evidence or offer reached the table.
What moved her: nothing; you showed her no document and owned nothing about the process, so she had no reason to shift.
What cost ground: thanking her for coming a second time instead of answering who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard first; to her a dodge on procedure looks like a school that punished first, and she got shorter.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because none was shown; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she opens by asking who decided and whether Owen was heard, say in one sentence that the zero went into the gradebook before anyone called her and that this was wrong, then go straight to your first dated piece of evidence.
